note: Re-confirmed 2026-09-08 after the functional-design redo jump, and re-saved following that confirmation. Coverage unchanged.

coverage.target: functional-spec.md > Workflow 1 step 2, and frontend-components.md > StepIndicator — 'Step X of Y' plus the named steps, not dots alone. Labels are the criterion rather than decoration: dots say how far, labels say what is left

functional-spec.md > Workflow 1 step 3, and frontend-components.md > OnboardingDraftStore — the human's Q1 = B decision. The draft persists in browser storage namespaced per account; where none was retained the field renders empty and visibly so. Restoring is conditional on the step still being current, so a stale draft is discarded rather than shown — a wrong prefill on a permanent property name is worse than an empty field. This closes user-stories reviewer finding R-02's first half

functional-spec.md > Workflow 1 step 7, and frontend-components.md > StepReview — prior steps open read-only and no control resubmits a completed step, because no route would accept the resubmission. The product gap the criterion NAMES — a mistyped property name is uncorrectable anywhere in the product — is not closed by any frontend behaviour and is recorded as a backend follow-up item; the review step makes the mistake visible before the final step commits, which is all it can do

functional-spec.md > Workflow 1 step 5, and frontend-components.md > Accessibility obligations — the saved indication is shown on each successful step transition and announced politely rather than signalled by colour alone

functional-spec.md > Workflow 1 step 8 — a completed account routes to the editor and never sees the wizard again. u4-owner-shell's Workflow 3 is what performs that routing, from the same onboarding read

functional-spec.md > Traceability. The wizard consumes ThemeTokens like every other surface, so no work in this unit is outstanding. Blocked on AC4.1.7: no frontend-reachable read returns a locality brand, so the functional default is what renders

frontend-components.md > ContentSourceStep — one action, 'Start from scratch', advancing to content review. The endpoint takes no body, and section authoring is not on this surface: the only way to write sections anywhere in the system is the guide PATCH

functional-spec.md > Workflow 1 ('No PDF upload control is rendered'), and frontend-components.md > ContentSourceStep — the control is absent rather than present-and-disabled. Verified stronger than the criterion states: the server does not parse PDFs at all, there is no upload endpoint, no multipart plugin, no object storage and no size limit, so a disabled control would advertise a feature whose entire implementation is missing

functional-spec.md > State machine, the saving-to-clean row — a successful save updates the last-loaded baseline, so a reload of the editor reads back what was sent. The full-replace semantics of the endpoint are what make this true rather than any merge logic here

functional-spec.md > Workflow 2 step 6, and frontend-components.md > SectionEditor — every save sends the complete section set under the exact expected key. Enforced in three layers: u1-api-contract's BR3.2 at the type level, u3-foundation's BR3.2 at run time before the request leaves, and this unit's ShrinkGuardDialog for the well-formed-but-unintended case

functional-spec.md > Workflow 2 step 5, and frontend-components.md > ShrinkGuardDialog — a save carrying fewer sections than the last loaded state confirms first, naming the count AND the section titles. A count alone is not enough to recognise a mistake by. The guard's limit is recorded rather than hidden: it compares against the last loaded state, so a stale load defeats it, and it guards the owner's own mistake rather than concurrency

functional-spec.md > Workflow 2 step 7b and the state machine's saving-failure row, and frontend-components.md > SectionEditor — the error shows, every edit stays on screen, nothing is silently discarded. The editor never clears itself on a failed write

functional-spec.md > What is settled, and frontend-components.md > API integration points — refetch-on-focus and prefetch are off. Enforced as client configuration by u3-foundation's BR3.5 rather than by per-component discipline, because the guide GET creates an empty draft row as a documented side effect

functional-spec.md > Workflow 3 step 2, and frontend-components.md > PublishControl — publishing shows the guide as published, with a persistent indicator beside the property name. Suppressed while the shell reports provisional
functional-spec.md > Workflow 3 step 2, and frontend-components.md > PublishControl — unpublishing returns the guide to draft. Same provisional suppression

functional-spec.md > Workflow 3 step 6, and frontend-components.md > GuestPreviewFrame. US1.8 is this unit's story, but the criterion describes what a GUEST sees, so it is realised in u9-guest-guide-view's placeholder rendering and reaches a guest through u8-guest-app. This unit's stake in it is that the same rendering is what the preview shows — which is precisely why Q2 = C extracted it rather than letting the owner preview a second copy that could drift from what guests actually receive. u8-guest-app declares the same criterion for the guest-facing half

functional-spec.md > Workflow 3 steps 4-6 and 'The ninth unit', and frontend-components.md > GuestPreviewFrame — the preview renders u9-guest-guide-view inside a labelled frame, so it is literally the guest rendering rather than a second copy of it. Per the human's Q2 = C decision. When nothing is published it shows the guest-facing placeholder exactly, never owner-framed wording
